cues: When hydroxide adds to the carbon carrying chlorine, the ring briefly holds an extra negative charge, before chloride leaves.
That charge moves around the ring, landing on the carbons ortho and para to the point of attack.
With a nitro group para, the charge reaches the nitro carbon and spreads onto its oxygens, so the intermediate is stabilised and the reaction is fast.
text: Here is why position matters. When hydroxide adds to the carbon carrying chlorine, the ring briefly holds an extra negative charge, before chloride leaves. That charge moves around the ring, landing on the carbons ortho and para to the point of attack. With a nitro group para, the charge reaches the nitro carbon and spreads onto its oxygens, so the intermediate is stabilised and the reaction is fast.
